annotation.material_differences: Response B omits the explicit “not to worry” reassurance and the claim that the replacement is basically on its way, but more importantly it does not preserve A/C’s stronger operational commitment to minimal proactive follow-up with updates only if something changes or there is a problem. C also adds an assumption that a likely delivery window can be based on normal turnaround and says the customer is effectively sorted, which is a stronger unsupported promise than B’s simpler “probably shipping soon.” These differences could affect expectation management and the follow-up mechanism criterion.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: A and C both make stronger reassurance/expectation-setting claims and specify that follow-up will be withheld unless there is a problem or change, while B is shorter and less detailed. The differences are not just brevity: B’s omission of the “effectively sorted”/“basically on its way” framing and of the more explicit no-update-until-change policy means it does not fully preserve the same decision-relevant evidence on expectation management and follow-up.
